predecessors.name: Emirate of Córdoba
predecessors.text: Badajoz and the west of al-Andalus (Gharb al-Andalus), from which Ibn Marwan, a Muladi noble expelled from Mérida, rebelled against Emir Muhammad I

successors.name: Caliphate of Córdoba
successors.text: Badajoz, whose lord 'Ibn Marwan of Badajoz' surrendered to Abd al-Rahman III in 930

ledger.x: c. 875: Ibn Marwan founds Badajoz as the seat of a rebel state. 'The official foundation of Badajoz was laid by the Muladi nobleman Ibn Marwan, around 875', after he was expelled from Mérida; 'Under Ibn Marwan, the city was the seat of an effective autonomous rebel state which was quenched only in the 10th century.'…
876-877: 'Between 876 and 877 he also erected the Castle of Marvão', in present-day Portugal; dated at the end of the span.
930: 'he achieved the surrender of Ibn Marwan of Badajoz in 930'; Ibn Marwan page: 'His dynasty lasted until 930.'
930: the Banu Marwan's rebel state ends.

wars.name: Revolt of Ibn Marwan
wars.outcome: Ibn Marwan rebelled in 868, won honourable surrender terms after prolonged resistance, was expelled from Mérida, founded Badajoz c.

certainty.note: The pages name towns and the 'throughout Gharb al-Andalus'; no boundary.
